answer: Each agent must lock a scarce token deposit before it can submit jobs or claim rewards; the contract records the deposit against one active identity and slashes it when independent auditors prove collusion or fabricated work. Spawning a hundred identities does not multiply influence for free: each needs its own capital, which is tied up and exposed to loss. A would-be sybil may forge credentials and seek a haven in anonymous accounts, but the attack reaches a nadir when the same deposit rule makes every fake identity costly to maintain.
